subject: Temporary contingency: content-filter routing and structured-output fallbacks for BrightCommerce
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@brightcommerce.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production incidents: personalization filter causing timeouts — need SLA contingency

Hi Rohan,

We're seeing an increase in 504s on our checkout personalization calls that route through Redwood's content filtering layer. The impact window is about 20-40ms added p50 but on some spikes we see timeouts that correlate with the filter tool-calls to the moderation endpoint. Engineering traced this to the structured-output path invoking two synchronous tool-calls; when one of the moderation instances returned slowly, the KV cache couldn't be used and requests timed out.

This is hitting conversion (2.1% drop in a 30-minute window) and our legal/ops team is asking for a short-term SLA tolerance so we can keep a non-blocking fallback while you push the fix. We're not asking to remove safety — only to allow a routing exception to a degraded-but-safe model variant when moderation latency exceeds X ms.

Can Redwood approve a temporary contingency (30 days) and provide a signed amendment that sets the operational conditions, rollback plan, and monitoring triggers?

Attached: sample-err.log showing the timestamps.

Thanks,
Jordan Ellis
Head of Platform, BrightCommerce
joe-signature-line

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@brightcommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production incidents: personalization filter causing timeouts — need SLA contingency

Jordan — thanks for the clear signal and the logs. Really sorry for the disruption.

Short answer: we can support a time-limited contingency for BrightCommerce with strict guardrails, provided Product & Legal align on the conditions. Proposed high-level controls:
- 30-day temporary routing exception to a fast, quantized model variant (no moderation removal).
- Auto-reversion if moderation latency drops below 150ms p95 for 10m or if errors exceed 0.5% for 5m.
- Enhanced telemetry and an audit trail for every routed fallback.

I'll loop in Ops to propose a concrete routing rule and the MCA (mutual change agreement). Marissa — can you put together the operational config and draft language for the amendment? Sean — can we scope the monitoring playbook and a one-click rollback?

Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Head of Sales (North America) | Redwood Inference

Thanks — drafting config now. Key implementation notes:

1) Routing rule (contingency): if moderation p95 > 250ms for the origin region for 3 consecutive 60s windows, route a copy of requests to a fast variant (quantized, lower latency) and send live traffic to the fast variant for up to 30 minutes. 
2) Structured-output fallback: change to non-blocking tool-invoke pattern (return best-effort JSON without blocking entire generation). This preserves structured fields used by BrightCommerce but avoids synchronous tool stall.
3) Telemetry: add explicit event flags (fallback.triggered=true) and include request_id, model_variant, and moderation_latency_ms in traces.

I've attached a contingency-routing diagram (contingency-routing-map.png) and a draft amendment (SLA_proposed_amendment_BrightCommerce.pdf). Legal will need to confirm the rollback indemnities.

Attachments:
- contingency-routing-map.png (image)
- SLA_proposed_amendment_BrightCommerce.pdf (pdf)

- Rohan: confirm commercial ask (credits / uptime SLO adjustment).

Quick update on monitoring/playbook:

- Alerting: create a composite that fires when (moderation.p95 > 250ms AND errors > 0.25%) sustained for 2m. Pager to SRE.
- Rollback: implement Console button that toggles routing to canonical variant; the endpoint flip uses atomic routing rules and logs the actor.
- Canary: we'll put the change behind a canary that starts at 1% traffic for 10m with synthetic traffic verifying structured-output fields are intact.

I'll prepare the ops-runbook and the Console change request today. Once Legal signs the amendment, we can schedule a 2-hour change window to apply the contingency.

Sean Gallagher
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
